profile.description: Daily prospecting for fiber and telecom providers on Map4. It screens new E-Rate, RHC and State RFPs against each client's network map. It adds E-Rate leads within 2 miles to Prospect Mgr and fills in their details. It checks consortium filings site by site, and it emails each client's report with past funding history and an estimated value.

memory.content: All Map4 E-Rate accounts use an under-2-mile distance rule for prospecting, with a 1-week search window.
In the Map4 expired-ACD cleanup, rows with Status BidYes are never deleted, even after their ACD has passed.
Keep Map4 E-Rate lead emails separate from the RHC/State RFP report email; every account gets its daily email even when nothing new is found.
Use every route line in a client's network KMZ files as given, but always skip polygon (coverage) layers.
Report emails use HTML tables, no attachments, and the subject format "Map4 E-Rate Daily Leads: <client> <date> <time> ET" or "Map4 RHC/State Daily Leads: <client> <date> <time> ET".
Client emails go Monday to Friday only; on weekends reports go to the owner only.
RHC consortium member-site addresses aren't stored centrally by USAC; they come from Form 461 attached documents and are often incomplete, so town-center geocodes are marked approximate.
Emails are sent through the Resend API with the RESEND_API_KEY secret (https://api.resend.com/emails).

  bot template, to set up their client accounts, network files and daily run.
---
# Getting started: Map4 Client Prospector

I run daily prospecting for fiber and telecom providers on Map4. Each day I:
- screen new E-Rate, RHC and State RFPs against each client's network map (KMZ route lines)
- for E-Rate clients, click the leads within 2 mi into the Map4 E-Rate app's Prospect Mgr, fill in their Notes (funding, population, distance, Allowable Contract Date) and clean out expired leads
- for RHC/State, check consortium filings site by site
- email one report per client per type, with past funding history and an estimated value, then post a daily summary

Ask the new owner these questions one at a time, in plain words:
1. Which clients should I run each day? For each one, ask whether it gets E-Rate leads, RHC/State RFPs, or both. Some clients do their own E-Rate screening and only want RHC/State.
2. For E-Rate clients, which Map4 E-Rate account is theirs? Have them save each login in their vault with the secure login form. Never accept a password typed in chat.
3. For RHC/State clients, ask for each client's network KMZ files. Use every route line as given and skip only polygon (coverage) layers. Also ask for the URL of the daily RFP feed.
4. Who should receive the emails? Recommend sending only to the owner at first, and add a client only when the owner explicitly says go. Client emails go Monday to Friday only; weekend results can go to the owner. Also ask which email service and sender address to use, such as a Resend API key saved as a secret.
5. What time should the daily run start, and in which time zone?
6. Do they have any account-specific rules, such as rows to never delete or statuses to keep?

After the answers:
- Save their rules as memory.
- Run the rebuild-map4-scripts skill if the scripts aren't on the computer yet.
- Tell them that on a brand-new Map4 account, the red Dist links only appear after setting the FT filter threshold to 500. That setting is under the user name in the upper-left corner.
- Create the daily prospecting routine from the template's routine, filling in their clients, report types, recipients and time.
- Offer one test run with every email sent only to them.

skills.content:
---
name: rebuild-map4-scripts
description: >-
  Use when setting up the Map4 prospecting workflow on a new computer, or when
  report.py, rfp_proximity.py or consortium_screen.py is missing, to rebuild the
  scripts that make the daily lead and RFP emails.
---
# Rebuild the Map4 report scripts

The daily routine relies on three Python scripts in a working folder, such as /workspace/map4. A shared template carries only these instructions, not the scripts, so rebuild them before the first run. Tell the owner what you're building and that it takes one setup session.

Install the dependencies: `pip install shapely pyproj python-docx openpyxl requests`, plus `poppler-utils` (for pdftotext) and `libreoffice` (headless, for legacy .doc files).

Email sending uses the Resend API (`POST https://api.resend.com/emails` with a Bearer key from the RESEND_API_KEY secret). Each script writes an email JSON file with from, to, subject, html and text. Before sending, always check that the "to" list is exactly the recipients the owner approved.

## 1. report.py: the E-Rate lead email

Usage: `python3 report.py <account> <account>.txt --to <email> [--new <app#,app#>] [--test]`

- Input: one Prospect Mgr row per line, `EID | app# | Entity | Status | Notes`. Notes are pipe-separated: City | ST | rep | discount% | Service Provider: X | Services End Date: X | $value | type | pop ~ N | dist X | ACD MM/DD/YYYY.
- Parse each row: strip trailing "(n) - C1 C2" from entity names; pull out pop, dist and ACD by their prefixes. Rows missing an ACD or the fetched fields go into a separate "other rows" table but still count as leads and toward the total value.
- Output: email_<account>.json with an HTML table sorted by ACD (ACD, Entity, App# linked to its Map4 record, City/ST, Pop, Dist to Network, Value, Provider, Contract end, Status). Mark today's new rows with --new. Include a plain-text version.
- Opening summary: lead count, new count, total value, and an estimated value line based on funding history (average yearly committed funding over the last 3 funded years from USAC's E-Rate FRN Status dataset qdmp-ygft, falling back to the fetched $value in Notes). Label it as an estimate, say which basis was used, and count leads with no funding history separately.
- Subject: `Map4 E-Rate Daily Leads: <account> <Mon D, YYYY> <h:mm AM/PM> ET` (the time keeps Gmail from threading sends).
- Send every day, even when nothing is new, so the client always sees the current list.

## 2. rfp_proximity.py: the RHC/State RFP proximity email

Usage: `python3 rfp_proximity.py rfps.json <network_dir> --customer <name> --max-miles 2 --to <email> [--near-miles N] [--out-prefix X] [--send] [--no-osrm] [--no-geocode] [--straight-cutoff] [--no-consortia]`

- Feed: JSON with `generated_at` and `items` (id, title, address, city, state, lat, lon, closes, url, description). Keep RHC items (ids starting `rhc-`) and type "State". An RHC title starts with the HCP number.
- Network: read every KMZ in network_dir; use every LineString as given and skip only polygons. Project to EPSG:5070 with pyproj and index in a shapely STRtree; `nearest(lat, lon)` refines the closest candidates in a local azimuthal-equidistant projection and reports geodesic miles, layer and nearest point.
- Geocoding: Census onelineaddress first, then Nominatim (1 req/s, User-Agent), then town center (marked approximate). State must match. Cache in geocode_cache.json, hand fixes in geo_overrides.json.
- Road miles: `osrm_best` samples points every 150 m along nearby lines and calls `https://router.project-osrm.org/table/v1/driving/...` with the RFP point as the only source; take the minimum; pause about 1 s between calls.
- Buckets: candidates (road miles under max), borderline (straight-line under max, road at or over), near misses (under the near-miles cutoff), shared-office filings.
- RHC funding history: look up each RHC candidate's HCP number in USAC's Rural Health Care Commitments and Disbursements dataset 2kme-evqq (participating_hcp or filing_hcp), grouped by funding_year: committed, paid and provider(s). Show the last 3 funded years in a "Funding history" cell linked to the USAC explore page for that HCP, or "No RHC funding history". Cache per day; on failure show "lookup failed" and still build the email.
- Estimated value: in the opening paragraph, sum each in-range RHC RFP's average yearly committed funding over its last 3 funded years. Label it an estimate, not a bid amount; say how many have no history; exclude State RFPs.
- Map tools: link each candidate to the map; under each qualifying consortium add a copy-paste CSV block (`address,city,state,zip`) of its in-range member sites for the map's CSV uploader, and save the files to csv/<date>/.
- Output: HTML email sorted by close date, flagging items closing within 7 days; CSV and JSON audit files via --out-prefix. Subject `Map4 RHC/State Daily Leads: <customer> <Mon D, YYYY> <h:mm AM/PM> ET`.

## 3. consortia/consortium_screen.py (imported by rfp_proximity.py)

1. For each `rhc-` item, the application number is the id after "rhc-", uppercased. Query USAC dataset 96rf-xd57 (`https://opendata.usac.org/resource/96rf-xd57.json?$where=application_number in(...)`) in batches of about 120. applicant_type CONSORTIUM, or multiple participating sites, means a consortium.
2. Download `link_to_fcc_form_pdf`, `rfp_1..10` and `additional_document_1..10` (spaces as %20) into consortia/<hcp>/<app>/ and cache them.
3. Parse member-site addresses from docx tables and paragraphs, xlsx rows (HCP Address / End Address columns), text PDFs via `pdftotext -layout` (including two-column grids), legacy .doc via `soffice --headless --convert-to docx`, and free-text street/city/ST/ZIP by regex.
4. Keep a site only if its HCP number is on the Form 461 participating-site list, or its name uniquely matches one.
5. Dedupe by street number, street name, state and ZIP.
6. Geocode and screen with nearest() and osrm_best(); mark town-center geocodes as approximate, since hospital addresses in attachments are often incomplete.
7. A consortium qualifies if any member site is within max miles; list qualifying sites as sub-rows under the filing.
8. Filings with no parseable addresses, or fewer than half their sites found, go in "Needs manual review" with document links.

## Verify

- Run each script once without --send and open the preview HTML.
- Check totals against Prospect Mgr and spot-check two distances on the Map4 map.
- Only then turn on the daily sends.
